decisions.reason: The changed sentence order keeps the same action and viewpoint.
“That perfect” preserves the ambush’s extreme perfection.
SOL keeps the unavoidable strike and the reason evasion is even less likely.
The singular “severe injury” conveys the source’s unavoidable serious harm.
SOL combines the next sentence’s survival-first point without changing its sense.
The sentence is retained in the preceding combined paragraph.
The revenge sentence is retained in the following combined paragraph.
SOL preserves the revenge resolve and the conditions under which he cannot die.
“Resume” naturally conveys returning to revenge after bringing down the immediate threat.
SOL makes clear what he is certain of and what he desperately hopes.
The dagger’s Force and its imminent strike remain clear.
The following sound description is combined here without dropping its effect.
The sound’s rush and the way it drowns out other noise are retained in H012.
The Eastern Heaven Demon Lord remains clear from context; SOL keeps the same arrival and visual effect.
“Only just noticed” preserves the delayed realization.
The spear’s slow-motion approach and coiling flames remain clear.
“Where … came from” naturally preserves the source’s question about the Qi’s origin.
SOL drops the source’s image of the spear crossing beyond a fleeting instant.
The last-moment dagger turn and block are preserved.
SOL keeps the blood-soaked appearance, quick movement, and grin.
The source places the dazed man at the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord’s feet, not merely beside him.
The source explicitly says he could not answer; SOL removes the stated action.
SOL preserves the silent gaze and laughter in natural English.
The tears are retained in the following paragraph.
The source says he grasped the Disciple’s arm tightly; “seized” drops that emphasis.
The source does not explicitly say “to me”; SOL preserves the return without adding it.
The recast preserves dried blood and the trembling eye corner.
“A few words” naturally conveys the brief utterance.
SOL preserves the warmth conveyed through the arm and the Master’s sincerity.
“More than enough” keeps the feeling’s complete significance.
The transition is tightened without changing the meaning.
“Mean death for their enemies” naturally preserves the impending consequence of the reunion.
SOL retains the three-hundred-year history and inexplicable Master-Disciple bond.
The source’s declaration is preserved without adding an explicit “we’ll.”
“Without fail” preserves the emphatic resolve.
SOL keeps their simultaneous advance and the killing intent wrapping around them.
“Cold” preserves the lack of agitation in his sunken eyes.
The disbelief is retained in the following combined sentence.
SOL combines the disbelief with the assassins’ identities and years of training.
“Himself” preserves that Heaven’s Slaughter could have killed Jeok Cheongang personally.
The broken wrist’s pain and the timing of the injury are preserved.
“Clearly from the darkness” preserves that he saw the event plainly while hidden there.
SOL retains the fatal injury, organ-filled blood, and death-shadow image.
The Korean states a general truth about martial artists; SOL shifts it into the past tense.
The tighter phrasing keeps the same claim that he knew this better than anyone.
“Since early childhood” preserves his very young age when trained and the weight of his deeds.
The recast preserves the miracle comparison and what Taekyung demonstrated.
Naming Taekyung explicitly resolves the pronoun from context without changing the fact.
“Seeped into” better preserves the source’s description of Force permeating his organs.
The generic Great Firmament Immortal and Yama’s impossible intervention remain intact.
The source says his perfect physique was confirmed; SOL’s “intact” adds a claim about its condition.
The amount of internal energy and his age remain faithful and clear.
“As easily as” adds ease; the source only compares the replenishment to filling a cup.
“Beyond reason” preserves the ability’s transcendence of ordinary logic.
“Trembled faintly” preserves the subtle tremor.
The source says his composure had collapsed, not merely begun to crumble.
The source presents flight and duty as the two alternatives he is torn between, not as an either-or choice.
SOL’s “between whose hands he would die by” is unidiomatic; BASE states the same question clearly.
The omitted subject is clear from context, and the offer’s lack of kindness remains.
“Accepted in exchange for his life” preserves the identity he took on to survive.
SOL keeps both the terrible pain and death beyond his imagining.
The inability to hide or flee is preserved.
The rephrasing preserves his self-reproach over a decision already settled.
The following sentence retains the sole-path idea, so this combination loses no meaning.
The single path is retained in the preceding combined paragraph.
“Painstakingly” preserves the care he put into raising the assassins.
“Either of them” and “just one” preserve the condition that taking down one target could let him survive.
SOL preserves both the unfulfilled revenge and his wish to keep living.
“Piercing sound” preserves the source’s sound of something splitting the air more directly than “rushing air.”
SOL drops the old-dragon image and the source’s detail that the breath came between his lips.
The source says he seemed to have forgotten his earlier prowess; “a far cry from” changes that image.
“Surpassed his limits” preserves the source’s description of exceeding his capacity.
Removing the connective “And” tightens the sentence without changing its meaning.
The energy of someone about to kill is preserved without the redundant “someone.”
The livestock comparison and absence of killing intent remain clear.
The recast preserves the butcher image and his identity as an assassin.
“Understood” preserves his realization at that same moment.
SOL’s “he” can refer to Taekyung; BASE makes clear Heaven’s Slaughter is the one still concealed.
